paragraphs.text: Anthropic sent bankers a copy of a securities filing on November 9, 2026, that priced its planned initial public offering at $70 to $80 per share, then retracted the pricing hours later, according to a Reuters report based on emails the news agency reviewed.

A follow-up email from the company told the same recipients that the pricing details were inaccurate and that an updated filing would come later. The email did not explain what was wrong, and Reuters said it could not determine the error. Anthropic declined to comment to Reuters.

The retracted version listed about 866.7 million Class A shares. Anthropic itself would sell roughly 843.3 million of them, and existing shareholders would sell about 23.3 million in a secondary offering. At the top of the price range, the sale would raise $69.3 billion, Reuters reported.

Shay Boloor of Futurum Equities estimated that the share count and price range implied a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, according to Stocktwits. Nasdaq Private Market currently values the company at $1.46 trillion, the same report said.

The filing also described $26 billion in commitments from large technology companies alongside the IPO. Alphabet's Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC agreed to buy Class N common stock in a private placement at the IPO price, closing right after the offering, according to Reuters.
A falling valuation and a tight schedule

Investors had earlier discussed a valuation of up to $2 trillion for the Claude developer. Reuters previously reported that $1.5 trillion is now seen as the high end, and Bloomberg reported talk of roughly $1.1 trillion to $1.3 trillion, according to Business Standard. Some potential investors wanted a better price before committing after a sharp sell-off in AI stocks following the US midterm elections.

Reuters said a formal roadshow was expected to start on Tuesday, November 10, with pricing the following week. The Wall Street Journal reported that Anthropic has investor meetings this week and aims to begin trading on Thursday or Friday of next week, though the company could still delay, Stocktwits noted.

The offering comes as other AI infrastructure and data center companies have delayed or withdrawn listings amid rising interest rates, and as shares and bonds of operators such as CoreWeave have sold off, Reuters reported.

Anthropic reported revenue of almost $17 billion for the three months ended September 30 in an amended filing earlier in November. Stocktwits, citing that filing, put third quarter growth at about 47 percent from the previous quarter, down from 144 percent in the second quarter, with a net loss of $23.29 billion for the period.

The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google, Reuters reported. Stocktwits put the total at $895.4 billion stretching to 2045, against about $146.6 billion in cash and other liquid assets.

A pulled price range is unusual for an offering of this size, and it lands at a sensitive moment. The figures in the retracted email were close to the valuation investors have been discussing, so the correction may be minor, but until the new filing appears the market has no official number to anchor on. The $26 billion placement from chip and cloud suppliers also shows how closely Anthropic's largest partners are tied to the outcome.
The next item to watch is Anthropic's updated filing with a corrected price range, which will show whether the company is still aiming near $1.4 trillion or has moved lower before trading begins.
